bluf.what: Nvidia's board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and a Board director effective 23 Nov 2026 -- roughly 11 days after his 11-12 Nov resignation amid a board inquiry into an alleged foreign-intelligence approach via a personal relationship linked to the Singapore chip firm Megaspeed. The board said it had consulted senior US government officials and is confident his return poses 'no national security risk'; its own independent investigation continues. Nvidia shares reportedly rose sharply (widely reported ~31%) on the news.
bluf.matters: This reverses the board's own 17 Nov statement that it had no plans to reinstate him, under reported pressure from President Trump and Elon Musk among others, while the underlying counterintelligence question remains formally open.
bluf.changes: Resets the leadership-continuity half of the AI/GPU vendor-risk picture this program flagged on 23-24 Nov, but does not resolve the compromise/export-control questions driving the Dec 1-10 congressional calendar.
bluf.needToKnow: Treat 'no national security risk' as the board's own characterization, informed by unnamed officials, not an independent clearance; Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to confirm or deny the investigation's status when asked.

bluf.what: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats will pursue a new congressional inquiry into the board's reinstatement process itself, on top of the already-scheduled House closed-door sessions with Huang (1 Dec) and Nvidia GC Tim Teter (2 Dec), Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott's invitation to Huang for roughly 3 Dec, and a separate Scott invitation to Commerce Secretary Lutnick for a public hearing around 10 Dec.
bluf.matters: The reinstatement adds a second, distinct oversight track (the board's own conduct) layered on the original espionage-adjacent and export-control questions, just as the hearing calendar this program flagged on 24 Nov comes due.
bluf.changes: A sharper, more partisan oversight environment heading into the 1-10 Dec window, rather than the reinstatement reducing scrutiny.
bluf.needToKnow: Whether Huang still appears on the stated dates, now as a sitting rather than ousted CEO, is the next concrete test.

items.observation: KNOWN: Ukrainian drones/missiles (reportedly incl. a Flamingo cruise missile) struck the Kerch Strait/Crimean Bridge on 16 and 17 Nov, collapsing a roughly 270-meter road-bridge span and damaging the adjacent rail bridge. items.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after forcing him out; Megaspeed's Entity-List status remains unresolved
items.observation: KNOWN (Nvidia's own 23 Nov SEC Form 8-K/press release): the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and a Board director effective immediately, citing candor and leadership ability and stating it consulted senior US officials and is confident his return poses 'no national security risk'; its own independent investigation continues. REPORTED: Nvidia shares rose sharply (widely cited ~31%) on the news; reporting ties the reversal to pressure from President Trump and Elon Musk following the board's own 17 Nov no-reinstatement statement. KNOWN: House Minority Leader Jeffries said Democrats will pursue a new inquiry into the reinstatement process itself. UNKNOWN/CLAIMED: separate press reports this week describe a Trump-administration move restricting Megaspeed's chip purchases, but this program could not independently confirm a formal BIS Entity List action; as of 13 Nov, Treasury Secretary Bessent said Commerce was still holding the listing.
items.context: This builds directly on the Nvidia CEO-resignation story this program caught up on 23 Nov and the Dec 1-10 congressional calendar flagged on 24 Nov.

redTeam.issue: Nvidia board's reinstatement of Jensen Huang while its own investigation remains open
redTeam.objection: A board that reverses a stated security-motivated decision within a week, under direct presidential pressure, while declining to say the investigation is closed, looks less like a resolved national-security judgment and more like a governance capitulation to political and market pressure -- treating 'no national security risk' as a credible finding may itself be the wrong call.
redTeam.response: The objection is well-founded and this brief does not treat the board's finding as independently verified; it explicitly separates the (now resolved) leadership-continuity question from the (still open) national-security and export-control questions, and recommends tracking each separately through the Dec 1-10 testimony window rather than accepting the board's characterization at face value.

No primary CISA KEV catalog page was independently reached this cycle, so this cycle's secondary-sourced KEV-addition claims (20, 23, and 24 Nov) remain unverified against the authoritative source.
Whether Zaporizhzhia NPP's 8 Nov external-power loss was restored the same day or has persisted since could not be reconciled this cycle.

competing: Nvidia board's 17 Nov 'no plans to reinstate' statement vs. its own 23 Nov reinstatement -- a genuine reversal, not merely conflicting reporting, but the underlying rationale (political pressure vs. a credible new finding) remains contested.
Whether the Berlin 'broader negotiating format' claim reflects genuine Russian flexibility or was always overtaken by the (then-unknown-to-this-program) Kerch Bridge strikes and Putin's harder line.
confidenceLimits: This cycle's research relied heavily on search-engine-synthesized secondary sourcing for several primary-source domains that were unreachable from this session's network, which this program flags per its own anti-fabrication standard rather than treating search-engine summaries as equivalent to primary verification.

forecastReview.priorForecast: fc-2026-11-23-nvidia-permanent-ceo: Nvidia's board will name a permanent CEO (distinct from interim CEO Colette Kress) within 180 days of Jensen Huang's 11 Nov 2026 resignation.
forecastReview.note: The board reinstated Jensen Huang himself as permanent President/CEO/Board director on 23 Nov 2026, just 12 days into the 180-day window -- a different outcome than most readers likely anticipated (a new successor), but one that satisfies the forecast's literal test: a permanent CEO, distinct from interim CEO Kress, was named well within the window.
